items.q: And so that was how I joined Fletcher. And I think when I joined Fletcher's band, I was

ctx.x: Yeah, when they were selling apples on the corner, 'brother can you spare a dime', you know, which I was blessed in that manner. And so that was how I joined Fletcher. And I think when I joined Fletcher's band, I was

maturing, you know. I was growing up and I was pretty much of a man by then, a man amongst men, because all these fellows who were in Fletcher's band, they had been around quite a bit. And I got to hear all the stories they used to tell about like Pop Smith and, you know, Coleman, Buster Bailey, and one of the other saxophone players, Harvey Boone. Used to tell us stories, you know, and I picked up on all the experiences, and they know how to handle themselves on the road and all that sort of thing. You know, I…
